Q: Why does Groq langchain model return 'tool use failed error'? A:

It's a malfunctioned call, notice the error you getting

<function=addTopic{"Topic": "Python Lists"}</function>

instead of structured json its a pseudo-XML format which resulted your error.
Would say simplify docstring for a fix
Also add a return value. Without return values agent loops can retry incorrectly.

This can sometimes happen when the tool schema is not very clear . Simplifying the tool definition along with returning a value can help agent handle the tool call correctly.

Example

@tool
def addTopic(Topic: str) -> str:
    """Adds a new coding topic to the TOPICS table. Topic should be a specific Python concept (e.g. 'List comprehensions', 'Decorators')."""
    connection = sqlite3.connect("learn.db")
    cursor = connection.cursor()
    cursor.execute(
        "INSERT INTO TOPICS(TopicID, Topic, Understood) VALUES(NULL, ?, 'False')",
        (Topic,)  
    )
    connection.commit()
    connection.close()
    return f"Topic '{Topic}' added successfully."

Q: Resource not found error when running miscrosoft semantic-kernel A:

Two issues here:

1. Deployment name vs model name confusion (the 404)

The "Resource not found" 404 means the endpoint is correct but the deployment name isn't matching what's actually deployed in Azure. The deployment name is what you named it in Azure AI Foundry (e.g. "my-gpt35-deployment"), not the model name ("gpt-35-turbo"). These are different things and it trips up almost everyone the first time.

Double check in Azure AI Foundry > Deployments that the name you're passing matches exactly, including casing.

2. The ValueError is a separate bug

create_semantic_function uses a text completion service by default, but AzureChatCompletion registers a chat service. They have different service IDs internally. This is why you get "TextCompletionClientBase service with service_id 'None' not found" — the kernel can't find a text completion service because you registered a chat one.

Fix — use create_semantic_function with the service ID explicitly, or switch to the chat-native approach:

kernel.add_chat_service("chat", AzureChatCompletion(

deployment_name=deployment, 

endpoint=endpoint, 

api_key=api_key

))

prompt = kernel.create_semantic_function(

"""Write a simple hello-world python program.""",

service_id="chat"

)

Also worth noting — this API (create_semantic_function, add_chat_service) is from a very old version of Semantic Kernel Python. The current SDK has changed significantly. If you're starting fresh, the current pattern uses Kernel() with AzureChatCompletion added via the kernel constructor and invokes functions differently.

if the credentials are definitely correct, the next thing to check is the API version. The old SK Python SDK was hardcoded to a specific Azure OpenAI API version internally, and if your deployment was created with a newer resource that version string no longer resolves — which returns a 404 even with valid credentials. Try explicitly passing api_version="2024-02-01" to the AzureChatCompletion constructor and see if that changes anything.

Q: What framework is used to enable cross-language communication in mozilla platform? A:

Mozilla uses XPCOM technology to integrate components written in different languages.

XPCOM is a cross platform component object model, similar to Microsoft COM. It has multiple language bindings, allowing XPCOM components to be used and implemented in JavaScript, Java, and Python in addition to C++. Interfaces in XPCOM are defined in a dialect of IDL called XPIDL.

XPCOM itself provides a set of core components and classes, e.g. file and memory management, threads, basic data structures (strings, arrays, variants), etc. The majority of XPCOM components are not part of this core set and are provided by other parts of the platform (e.g. Gecko or Necko) or by an application or even by an extension.

Q: Is Java still worth learning to get a job soon? Seniors — please spit the truth A:

Instead of asking strangers on the internet, lookup jobs matching your experience and qualification, and see what sort of skills those ask for. In other words, use data already available instead of speculation.

Q: KrbException: Do not have keys of types listed in default_tkt_enctypes available A:

It's complaining that you used an incompatible algorithm when creating the keytab. When creating the keytab. I usually use RC4-HMAC:

kutil
addent -password -p username@MYDOMAIN.COM -k 1 -e RC4-HMAC
wkt username.keytab
quit

Now it works fine.

Q: The transaction log for database is full due to 'log_backup' / (Log)LDF file 4 times bigger than (Data)MDF A:

You are basically answering your own question, all you need to do is choose one option.

I am guessing your recovery model is full: this means that ALL your transactions will be written to the log file for 'point in time restore'. That is why your log file is so big and unless you:

  • back it up and shrink the log file
  • change recovery model to simple and shrink the log file

it will stay that way.

The 2 solutions are more or less equivalent. There is a small risk in the latter option of having no way to do a point in time restore if your server crashes right after you change the recovery model and shrink the file, but I am guessing that is a 0,(0)1 possibility and not an issue since you backups are not properly set up.

In either situation, if you decide to leave your recovery model set to full make sure you include the log in some sort of a regular backup, otherwise you (or somebody else) are going to have this problem again somewhere in the future.

Q: Can't find out my url in Jboss server A:

Once you deploy the application, in your local environment. Open the location inside(eg:\Serveur\jboss\4.2.2.GA\server.) where your .ear file has been created. Open META-INF folder and you will find application.xml. Here whatever is mentioned within the tags MyApplication is your application path.

Your final url would be: localhost:8080/MyApplication

Q: Rate limit error while using Azure chat playground with data source and system message A:

The issue is token inflation from the RAG pipeline, not your quota being too low.

When you add a data source in the Azure OpenAI playground, each request silently includes:

Your system message

The retrieved chunks from Azure AI Search (can be 2,000-8,000 tokens per query depending on your index configuration)

The conversation history

Your actual user message

What looks like a simple chat message is consuming 5-10x more tokens than a plain API call. At 100K TPM with GPT-3.5-turbo that headroom disappears fast, especially in the playground where you might not realize each test click is a full retrieval + completion cycle.

Immediate fixes:

In the playground's data source settings, reduce the number of retrieved documents — default is often 5, drop it to 2 or 3. This directly cuts the token cost per request.

Shorten your system message if it's long. Every token in the system prompt multiplies across every request.

If this is for production:

100K TPM is the right starting point but you'll likely need to request higher quota once you understand your actual per-request token consumption. Check the usage tab in Azure AI Foundry after a few requests to see real token counts.

Also implement retry logic that reads the Retry-After header from the 429 response:

if (ex.Status == 429)

{

var retryAfter = ex.GetRawResponse()

    .Headers.TryGetValue("Retry-After", out var val)

    ? int.Parse(val) : 10;

await Task.Delay(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(retryAfter));

}

Full retry and circuit breaker pattern for Azure OpenAI 429s: https://www.dotnetstudioai.com/hospital/fix-429-rate-limit-exceeded-azure-openai-dotnet
